ordinance: Pittsburgh Zoning Ordinance of 1923, as amended in 1926 and 1927, with its zone map corrected to August 1927
map_title: City of Pittsburgh Zoning Map, adopted July 1923 and amended through August 1927, digitized by Details Reviewed (Western Pennsylvania Regional Data Center, CC BY)
structure: Three separate sets of districts: use, height and area. Each polygon here carries one of each. Colors show the use district; choose height or lot area under Color by.
hierarchy: Use rules run from one-family houses only (C Residence) to nearly any use (Heavy Industrial). Height and area limits are set separately.
method: Boundaries are the published digitization, clipped to land, and were not read from a scan for this atlas. Parks are shown with the district the digitized map gives them. Rules come from the 1923 ordinance and from the 1926 and June 1927 amendments printed in the Pittsburgh Municipal Record; side-yard rules and other amendments through August 1927 are not included. Each of today's tax parcels (Allegheny County, October 2026) takes the district covering most of it, and parcels are merged by census block for this map. Today's lots are not the lots of 1927.
boundary_rule: Sec. 47: boundaries are streets unless shown otherwise, then lot lines, then by the map's scale.

form_notes.lot_sqft_per_unit: Shown for one-family houses; multiple dwellings could use less per family.

height_districts.H-4: 125 ft and 10 stories; dwellings other than hotels, apartment houses and club houses are held to 100 ft (Sec. 23).
height_districts.H-5: 265 ft and 21 stories, and towers may go higher; dwellings other than hotels, apartment houses and club houses are held to 100 ft (Secs. 24, 29).

area_districts.A-1: Lot per family: one-family 4,000 sq ft; double house or two-family 2,500. Front yard 15 ft; rear yard 15% of lot depth, up to 25 ft (Sec. 32).
area_districts.A-2: Lot per family: one-family 2,500 sq ft; double house or two-family 1,875; multiple dwelling up to 3 stories 1,250, over 3 stories 750. Front yard 15 ft; rear yard 15% of lot depth, up to 25 ft (Sec. 33).
area_districts.A-3: Lot per family: one-family 2,000 sq ft; double house or two-family 1,500; multiple dwelling up to 3 stories 1,000, over 3 stories 625. Rear yard 15% of lot depth, up to 15 ft (Sec. 34).
area_districts.A-4: Lot per family: one-family 1,500 sq ft; double house or two-family 1,125; multiple dwelling up to 3 stories 600, over 3 stories 400. Rear yard 15% of lot depth, up to 15 ft (Sec. 35).
area_districts.A-5: Lot per family: one-family 1,200 sq ft; double house or two-family 900; multiple dwelling up to 3 stories 400, over 3 stories 250. Dwellings need a rear yard of 15% of lot depth, up to 15 ft; other buildings need none (Sec. 36).

zones.name: C Residence District
zones.summary: One-family houses only. Added in September 1926 (Ordinance No. 449), this was Pittsburgh's first exclusive single-family district.
permitted_uses: Accessory uses as in the A Residence District

zones.name: B Residence District
zones.summary: One- and two-family houses and double houses. Apartments are not allowed.
permitted_uses: School, including faculty and student dormitories
Minor garage or stable set back at least 60 ft from the front lot line
Small sale or lease signs and name plates

zones.name: A Residence District
permitted_uses: Multiple dwellings, Class A and Class B
Public or semi-public educational or charitable institution
Telephone exchange, electric substation without rotary machinery, gas regulating station
Minor garage or stable set back at least 60 ft from the front lot line
Small sale or lease signs and name plates
conditional_uses: On a Major Street Plan street in Area District A-3 or A-4, a multiple dwelling of 8 or more stories may sell goods at retail on the ground floor, with the written consent of a majority of owners within 100 ft (Sec. 13-A, as amended June 1927)

zones.name: Commercial District
zones.summary: Any use except those listed as barred, which include most manufacturing, major garages and gasoline stations.
excluded_uses: Everything barred in Light Industrial
Automobile wrecking yards; major garages; gasoline service stations
Blacksmith shops; brick, tile and terra cotta manufacture; stone or monument works
Carpet or bag cleaning; coal and coke storage; contractors' plants; lumber yards; storage warehouses
Brewing or distilling; milk bottling; oiled or leather goods manufacture; major stables; saw, planing or woodworking mills; repair shops other than carpenter shops without machinery
Manufacturing, unless most of the product is sold at retail on the premises
permitted_uses: Any use not listed as barred

zones.name: Light Industrial District
zones.summary: Any use except heavy or noxious industry. Dwellings are allowed.
excluded_uses: Everything barred in Heavy Industrial, except dwellings
Acid, chlorine, asphalt, celluloid, creosote, dyestuff, glue, match, paint, varnish, potash, printing ink, tar and soda manufacture
Blast furnaces, rolling mills, smelters, coke ovens, boiler works, iron or steel foundries
Petroleum refining and bulk petroleum or gasoline storage
Gas manufacture or storage over 10,000 cubic feet
Fat rendering; soap, tallow and grease manufacture
Junk, scrap, metal, paper or rag storage
Paper and pulp, oil cloth, linoleum, rubber manufacture
Rock crushing; tanning and storage of raw hides
In general, uses noxious or offensive by odor, dust, smoke, gas, vibration or noise
permitted_uses: Any use not listed as barred, including dwellings

zones.name: Heavy Industrial District
zones.summary: Any use except a short list of the most noxious trades. Dwellings are barred, except watchmen's quarters.
excluded_uses: Abattoirs
Cement, lime, gypsum or plaster of Paris manufacture
Dwellings, except quarters for watchmen and their families at an industrial site
Animal fertilizer manufacture
Gunpowder, fireworks or other explosives
Incineration, reduction or storage of garbage, offal, dead animals or refuse
Pyroxyline plastic manufacture
Stock yards
permitted_uses: Any use not listed as barred
